changes: p1 name: removed the Newari honorific -ju, so 'Dhaṃsi' (kept as a variant in notes); titles now bhāju and ju
p3: name read as 'Jio Dhaṃ' (Newari honorific -ju removed) and confidence lowered to medium; the split of 'jio dhaṃju' is uncertain
All five persons get the role 'beneficiary' because of 'thuti sayāṃ maṅgala juya māra' (may all these be blessed); p1 stays donor (dānapati)
place: emptied. 'hataṣāde onani' is given as the donor's residence, not as the place of copying; it stays in p1's residence field
purpose: changed from a fragment of the Newari to its meaning
date: tithi stays ṣaṣṭhī; added yathākaraṇa muhūrta, Sun in Makara and Moon in Meṣa; notes on the CE year and the conflict with the catalogue's 910

date.as_written: samvat 950 mti māghamāsya śuklapakṣe ṣaṣṭammītithau aśuṇinakṣatre, śubhayogya yathākarṇṇamahātre, ādityavāsare, makrarāsigate śavitre meṣarāsigate candraṃmasi
date.nakshatra_yoga: aśvinī nakṣatra, śubha yoga; yathākaraṇa muhūrta; Sun in Makara, Moon in Meṣa

purpose: Pious gift (dānapati) by Dhaṃsi and family; ends with Newari 'thuti sayāṃ maṅgala juya māra' = may all these (the named family) be blessed
notes: The catalogue gives the year as NS 910, but the quoted colophon reads 'samvat 950'. The colophon reading has been followed, though the catalogue figure may be the correct one. NS 950 + 880 = 1830. However, Māgha falls in January–February, so the actual date is probably early 1831 CE. Sun in Makara with Moon in Meṣa/Aśvinī on śukla 6 fits Māgha. 'hataṣāde onani' is unclear: perhaps a locality (tole) followed by a Newari locative or verb form. It is recorded as the donor's residence, not as the place of copying. 'bhāju' and '-ju' are Newari honorifics, so the stems are Dhaṃsi (also possible: Dhaṃsiju) and Jio Dhaṃ. The split of 'jio dhaṃju' is uncertain; it might be a single name, Jiodhaṃ. 'vilalakṣmi' might be a corruption of Vilāsalakṣmī. No scribe is named.
